```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = "##", fig.align = "center")
library(NNS)
```

There was a recent image that was posted^[<http://www.datasciencecentral.com/profiles/blogs/machine-learning-summarized-in-one-picture>],
and NNS' seamless integration of the identified tasks (clustering, regression,
and classification) in machine learning was apparent. It is a regression based
on clusters!

# Clustering

> Reference: Clustering and Curve Fitting by Line Segments,
> <https://ssrn.com/abstract=2861339>

The first step of NNS regression (`NNS.reg`) is to iteratively partition the
data into partial moment quadrants and assign a sequential quadrant number to
each observation. It is both a partitional and hierarchical clustering.

Below is a visualization of the unsupervised NNS partitioning (`NNS.part`) and
the resulting clusters (red points):

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
require(devtools)
install_github('OVVO-Financial/NNS', ref = "NNS-Beta-Version")
require(NNS)
```

```{r partition, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "NNS partition and clustering"}
x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, pi / 1000); y <- sin(x)
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
for (i in 1:6) {
  NNS.part(x, y, order = i, obs.req = 1, Voronoi = TRUE)
}
```

# Regression

> Reference: Nonparametric Regression Using Clusters,
> <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10614-017-9713-5>

`NNS.reg` uses the `NNS.part` clusters as the basis of a nonlinear
nonparametric regression.

## Univariate regression

```{r univariate, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "NNS regression sequence of orders in univariate example."}
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
for (i in 1:6) {
  NNS.reg(x, y, order = i, noise.reduction = "off", residual.plot = FALSE)
}
```

## Multivariate regression

NNS extends this partitioning and clustering to higher dimensions for a
complete multivariate analysis.

```{r multivariate-data}
f <- function(x, y) x^3 + 3 * y - y^3 - 3 * x
x <- seq(-5, 5, 0.1); y <- seq(-5, 5, 0.1)
z <- expand.grid(x, y)
g <- f(z[, 1], z[, 2])
```

The regions at each order are drawn in an interactive 3-D device:

```{r multivariate-regions, eval = FALSE}
for (i in 1:6) {
  NNS.reg(z, g, plot.regions = TRUE, order = i)
}
```

Multivariate $\hat{Y}$ vs. $Y$ plot:

```{r multivariate-fit, fig.cap = "NNS multivariate regression fitted vs. actual values."}
fit <- NNS.reg(z, g, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy
plot(fit$y, fit$y.hat, pch = 19, cex = .3, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Y", ylab = expression(hat(Y)))
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

# Classification

> Reference: Classification Using NNS Clustering Analysis,
> <https://ssrn.com/abstract=2864711>

`NNS.reg` is also applicable to classification methods and for smaller
dimensions will report the same output as a k-nearest neighbor algorithm (KNN)
when both are set to k = 1 under specific NNS settings (limit condition whereby
every observation is its own cluster). NNS does not have the same restrictions
as KNN, such as using an odd numbered k to avoid ties.

The above reference demonstrates several classification tasks from Iris, UCI
Wine dataset, an XOR classification, the Cassini dataset and a text
classification example.

> **Note (2026).** The original version compared NNS and KNN on MNIST and
> reported a 75% reduction in error rate. That figure was one reported run
> without a matched KNN fit, and the comparative and dimensionality claims are
> withdrawn pending common splits, preprocessing, tuning, metrics and repeated
> runs (see `examples/example-corrections.md`).

# Time-Series Forecasting

> Reference: Forecasting Using NNS, <https://ssrn.com/abstract=3382300>

`NNS.reg` has also been integrated into a time-series forecasting routine.
Regressions are performed on seasonal components, without the need for
stationarity or ACF / PACF analysis.

For examples of `NNS.ARMA`, see the examples directory:
<https://github.com/OVVO-Financial/NNS/tree/NNS-Beta-Version/examples>

```{r forecast, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "NNS seasonal periods and resulting forecast."}
x <- seq(0, 30, .01); y <- sin(x)
invisible(NNS.ARMA(y, h = 1000, negative.values = TRUE, method = "lin"))
```
